solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dad’s chant helping at football?

blocks.note: Pa is an informal word for dad, with the possessive ’s kept
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A father's terrace song is cheering his team on at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole clue as one phrase about singing in the stands; the split is after the possessive, which supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing the ball to a teammate is the way a footballer helps another player, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Monster standing in wood spiked rodent

indicators.note: in says the monster and its standing sit inside the wood

blocks.note: an orc is a fantasy monster
standing means up on one's feet
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A monster lurks upright in a forest beside a prickly animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a rodent covered in sharp quills, so spiked describes it exactly.

clue.text: Second row finding it difficult to move

blocks.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel, as is a tiff

explanation.surface: Someone in the second row of seats struggles to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: Row reads as a line of seats, but here it is the quarrel sense, said to rhyme with cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff joint, drawer or limb is one that resists motion and will not bend easily.

clue.text: Rather snide at parties

indicators.note: to party is to let loose and carouse, so the letters go wild and rearrange

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone is rather sarcastic when out at social gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: Parties looks like a noun, but it is a verb acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather can mean in place of, as in tea rather than coffee, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Country led by old king rather than almost intelligent president

indicators.note: led by puts the other pieces in front of the country
almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the cipher of King George
choosing one thing over another means rather than it
intelligent means clever; the last letter is then dropped
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A nation is ruled by a former monarch instead of a not-so-bright head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex, seen on postboxes. The surface suggests politics, but the president is the 22nd and 24th of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland served two non-consecutive terms as President of the United States.

clue.text: Swiss girl at altitude called out greeting to campers

indicators.note: called out means spoken, so we want what the phrase sounds like rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Heidi is the Swiss girl of the children's novel, and at altitude is high

explanation.surface: A Swiss girl up in the mountains shouts a welcome to people camping.
explanation.walkthrough: Hi-de-Hi! was a British sitcom set in a 1950s holiday camp, named after the greeting staff called to the campers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-de-hi was the call staff at British holiday camps such as Butlins used to welcome guests.

clue.text: Troll biting heads off mice and squirrels, 1 Down’s relative?

indicators.note: heads off means the leading letter is taken from each of the following words
something biting holds what it bites between its jaws, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an internet troll is a hater who posts abuse
first letters of mice and squirrels

explanation.surface: A monster snaps the heads off small woodland creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Troll suggests a fairytale monster, but here it is the online sense. 1 Down is the porcupine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the hamster and the porcupine are rodents, so one is a relative of the other; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Clock-maker adjusted dial on end

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A watchmaker repositions a clock face on its end.
explanation.walkthrough: Clock-maker evokes a craftsman, but a dandelion clock is the fluffy seed head children blow to tell the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant produces the round seed head known as a clock, so it is literally what makes one.

clue.text: Noodles, nuts or beans in sailor’s can?

blocks.note: first meaning: slang words for the top part of the body, plural
second meaning: a ship's lavatory, can being slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A shopping list of foods stored in a sailor's tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about tinned provisions at sea; can is the American slang for toilet, and the naval word for one is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle, nut and bean are all slang for the skull, and a ship's toilets are traditionally called by the same plural word.

clue.text: Brit on Mars struggling to have many ideas

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A British astronaut on Mars finds it hard to come up with lots of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainstorm is to generate a flood of suggestions quickly, usually as a group exercise.

clue.text: Orderly area inside court barrier

indicators.note: inside places the area within the barrier

blocks.note: a is the abbreviation for area
the net divides a tennis court

explanation.surface: A tidy space is fenced off inside a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests a law court, but the barrier is the net across a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and orderly are close synonyms describing something tidy and well arranged.

clue.text: Trump emptied fake tan bottles — spoon’s beginning to stir things up

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the outer ones
bottles means holds inside, as a bottle encloses its contents
beginning picks out just the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: in card games, to ruff is to play a trump
to tan someone's hide is to leather, or thrash, them
outside letters of fake
first letter of spoon

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a fake-tanned Trump and a spoon stirring trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the politician but the card-game verb, and tan means beat. The emptied fake sits inside the beating word, then the spoon's first letter ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle feathers is an idiom for annoying or upsetting people, causing a stir among them.

clue.text: Aristocratic idiot given guidance

blocks.note: tit is British slang for a fool
someone given guidance has been led

explanation.surface: A foolish nobleman is being steered by an advisor.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats hold titles such as duke or earl, so a titled person belongs to the nobility.

clue.text: Large lady in opera dies horribly, rejected

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled and disfigured, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
Aida is the title heroine of Verdi's opera
the fodder letters for the anagram

explanation.surface: A large soprano in an opera has a gruesome death scene and is spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the old saying about the fat lady singing at the end of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid aside has been put away or discarded, which is to say it was not wanted.

clue.text: Four squeezed into corporal’s Fiesta

indicators.note: squeezed into means pressed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: corporal and carnal both mean of the body
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four soldiers cram into an army corporal's small Ford car.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporal looks like an army rank and Fiesta like the Ford model; here corporal is the adjective meaning bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or public celebration, the same thing as a carnival with parades and revelry.

clue.text: Big arms worse in painting, perhaps Hockney’s last?

indicators.note: last picks out only the final letter of the name
in places the comparative inside the other pieces

blocks.note: painting is an example of art, hence perhaps
ill means bad, so worse can be iller
last letter of Hockney

explanation.surface: A query whether David Hockney's latest painting is a worse effort.
explanation.walkthrough: David Hockney is a British painter. ART and Y join first, and the comparative of ill goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery means large-calibre guns such as cannons, as opposed to small arms carried by soldiers.

clue.text: Pedestrian’s first person Detective Inspector Brown picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the sound counts

blocks.note: me is the first person pronoun
DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector
ochre is a brownish-yellow earth colour

explanation.surface: A police detective named Brown is pulled over by a walker.
explanation.walkthrough: Pedestrian looks like a walker, but it is the adjective meaning dull. Brown looks like an inspector's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing or work is dull and uninspired, which is what ordinary second-rate quality means.

clue.text: Musical instrument in case secured by screw as missing odd bits

indicators.note: missing odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters go, keeping the even ones
secured by means held fast inside the other piece

blocks.note: even letters of screw as
lest means in case, as in take a coat lest it rain

explanation.surface: An instrument packed in its case with screws, some fiddly parts missing.
explanation.walkthrough: In case is not a container signal but the wordplay itself, meaning lest; the kept letters of screw as wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal bars, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Utter fool has broken marbles

definitions.note: plural slang noun, treated as a mass noun for one's mental faculties

indicators.note: has broken means has burst into the middle of the other word, splitting it

blocks.note: to utter is to say
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A complete idiot has smashed a set of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Utter looks like an adjective describing the fool, but it is the verb meaning speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose your marbles is an idiom for going mad, so marbles stands for a sound mind.

clue.text: Knack of walking on water working less with age

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over or kneaded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters of less and age, joined by with

explanation.surface: A miracle-worker finds walking on water works less well as they get older.
explanation.walkthrough: Walking on water evokes a miracle, but it means staying steady on a ship's deck at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep balance and avoid seasickness aboard a moving vessel.

clue.text: Coiffed crimefighters from Lancashire swapped hair products

indicators.note: swapped means the letters have traded places, so they appear in a different order

blocks.note: the fodder letters; Lancashire is a county in north-west England
gels are styling products for hair

explanation.surface: A Lancashire salon trades styling products to glamorous detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England. Coiffed nods to Farrah Fawcett's famous hairdo in the 1970s TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie's Angels were three glamorous private detectives in the TV show and films, famous for their styled hair.

clue.text: Conservative leader in Kuwait returned battery, say

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the Kuwaiti leader's title reads backwards

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Kuwait is ruled by an emir

explanation.surface: A Tory leader in Kuwait sends back a battery, perhaps a faulty one.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests a power cell, but the legal sense from assault and battery is meant, so say marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery, unlawful physical attack on someone, is an example of an offence against the law.

clue.text: Twisted round, did telephone line knot?

indicators.note: twisted round means turned back the other way, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tangled telephone cord got tied in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: Twisted and knot both suggest the phone cord; the definition is the question-marked last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnarl is a rough knotty growth on a tree trunk, the same as a knot in wood.

clue.text: Flightless bird of legend, tiny one hears

indicators.note: one hears means as someone would hear it spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a map's legend is its key, and wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: A tiny mythical bird that cannot fly, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend suggests myth, but it is the key that explains a map's symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi of New Zealand is a small bird with vestigial wings that cannot fly.

clue.text: Someone on a trip apparently walked around California in circle

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the walking word wraps the state abbreviation
in places the combined piece inside the circle

blocks.note: a circle of friends is a set
paced means walked up and down
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A traveller paced about California in a loop.
explanation.walkthrough: On a trip suggests travel; here it is a drug trip, with apparently signalling the joke about trainee astronauts.
explanation.definitionFit: A space cadet is slang for a dreamy, spaced-out person who seems to be tripping, literally a trainee astronaut.

clue.text: Information Age classes for biologists

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is an age

explanation.surface: The Information Age has courses in biology.
explanation.walkthrough: Information Age reads as one phrase, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are taxonomic ranks grouping related species, used by biologists to classify living things.

clue.text: Screen underworld drama

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A film studio decides to show a dark crime drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen looks like a noun for a monitor, but it is the verb, as in screening a film.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a film or programme is to show it publicly, so the two verbs are synonyms.
